G-ROP_1.headline: Set up your record of processing activities
G-ROP_1.teaser: What you do with personal data, one line per activity.
G-ROP_1.fromNis2: Your asset list from NIS 2 suggests the activities here. NIS 2 records your systems and how much they matter to the business; this record says what you do with personal data: the purpose, whose data, which data, who receives it and when it is erased (Art. 30(1)).
missed: The exemption for companies employing fewer than 250 persons (Art. 30(5)) almost never applies. Any one of three conditions removes it: the processing is likely to result in a risk to the people concerned, it is not occasional, or it includes special categories of data or data on criminal convictions and offences. A monthly payroll is not occasional.
The supervisory authority can ask for the record (Art. 30(4)). Change it as soon as an activity is added or dropped.
Where possible, the record also holds a general description of your security measures (Art. 30(1)(g)). The step on security of processing writes it; the record can refer to it.

learn.title: What you do with data
body: The record lists every processing activity of your company, such as payroll, customer management, the website or video surveillance. For each it says what you process the data for, whose data and which, who receives it, whether it goes to a country outside the EEA and when it is erased (Art. 30(1)). It also names your company and your data protection officer, with contact details.
In writing here includes electronic form (Art. 30(3)).

On the next steps you choose your activities from a list and describe each one. Every entry comes with a suggestion you can use or change. If your data protection officer already keeps a record, put it next to this one and compare the two.
learn.duty: The GDPR requires your company to maintain a record of the processing activities under its responsibility.

line.title: What a line looks like
line.caption: A made-up line for payroll:

rows.name: Purpose
rows.detail: Calculate and pay wages, pay over income tax and social security contributions

rows.name: Categories of data
rows.detail: Name, address, bank details, tax ID, social security number, salary, tax class

rows.name: Specially protected data
rows.detail: Yes: religious affiliation, for German church tax

rows.name: Recipients
rows.detail: Tax adviser, tax office, health insurers, bank

rows.name: Erasure
rows.detail: Payroll accounts until the end of the sixth calendar year after the last payment (§ 41(1) EStG), accounting vouchers eight years (§ 147(3) AO)

line.note: The GDPR does not say how detailed a line must be. It should show what happens to the data.

staff.title: Your staff
staff.lead: What do you do with the data of your staff and applicants? Tick what applies to you.

customers.title: Customers and suppliers
customers.lead: What do you do with the data of customers, prospects and suppliers? Your contacts at business customers are people with data too.

online.title: Online
online.lead: Website, newsletter, social media and video meetings. Tick what your company uses.

operations.title: Running the company
operations.lead: Email, your IT's logs, access control and cameras. Security measures process personal data too, for example the logs your IT writes of every sign-in.

what.title: What for, whose data, which data
what.lead: Each activity comes with a suggestion. Use it, or write how it is for you. Write groups, such as staff or customers, not the names of individual people.

basis.title: On what lawful basis
basis.lead: Why may you use this data? The law allows it only for one of six reasons (Art. 6(1)). Most activities rest on one of two: you need the data for a contract with the person, such as an employment contract or an order, or a law makes you keep it, such as tax law. The usual reason for each activity is marked; take it unless your case is different. Consent fits only where the person has a genuine choice and can withdraw it at any time (Recital 42, Art. 7(3)). Website tools that store or read information on a visitor's device need consent unless they are strictly necessary (§ 25 TDDDG). If you rely on legitimate interests, write in one sentence what your company needs, and why the interests of the people concerned do not override it.

who.title: Who receives the data
who.lead: A recipient is anyone you disclose the data to, your service providers included (Art. 4(9)). Tick the suppliers that receive the data, then name the other recipients. Whether data leaves the EEA through a supplier is recorded once for that supplier; here you only say whether it leaves another way.

keep.title: When data is erased
keep.lead: Personal data may be kept only as long as necessary for the purpose (Art. 5(1)(e)). Where a law sets a retention period, the suggestion names it. Where none does, you set the period yourself.

done.title: Your record is set up
done.note: When an activity is added or dropped, change the record. You find it at any time under Record of processing activities.
